CVE-2026-96236 (GHSA-f4g7-52wc-p8x7) is an ASP.NET Core denial of service in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Localization: when RequestLocalizationMiddleware falls back to parent cultures, request-supplied culture names that are well formed but not predefined (for example fr-FR-a0000001-b0000001-c0000001-d0000001-e0000001) are created and kept in the runtime's global culture cache, so unauthenticated requests can grow memory without bound. Microsoft lists the ASP.NET Core 10.0 runtime packs, including linux-x64 and linux-arm64, as affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 and fixed in 10.0.13: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-f4g7-52wc-p8x7, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/484, https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69803, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md. The .NET 10 fix is dotnet/dotnet commit e4eb9f4add4c489054e5fd7a9be8322388a94174 ('Reject non-predefined cultures in request localization fallback'), which changes the fallback lookup in RequestLocalizationMiddleware.cs from CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo(name) to CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo(name, predefinedOnly: true); it is in the v10.0.113 source tag and not in v10.0.112: https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/commit/e4eb9f4add4c489054e5fd7a9be8322388a94174. DHI dotnet-sdk-10 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's .NET 10 SDK for Linux, which includes the ASP.NET Core shared framework. We checked every package built from this source and published in the DHI Debian repository by 2026-11-28: dotnet-sdk-10 10.0.301-0, 10.0.302-0, 10.0.302-1, 10.0.400-1, 10.0.401-0, 10.0.401-1, 10.0.402-0, 10.0.403-0, 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1 for amd64 and arm64, and the dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages, which hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog; no debug-symbol packages are published. The file list and checksums of each dotnet-sdk-10 package show two files named Microsoft.AspNetCore.Localization.dll: the implementation in the ASP.NET Core shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App/<version>, and a reference assembly in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref targeting pack, which carries metadata for compilation and no method bodies. In every build the shared-framework copy is byte-identical (same MD5) to Microsoft.AspNetCore.Localization.dll in Microsoft's Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.linux-x64 or linux-arm64 NuGet package of the same version: 10.0.9 in 10.0.301-0, 10.0.10 in 10.0.302-0 and 10.0.302-1, 10.0.11 in 10.0.400-1, 10.0.12 in 10.0.401-0 and 10.0.401-1, 10.0.13 in 10.0.402-0, 10.0.14 in 10.0.403-0, and 10.0.15 in 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1. Reading the assembly metadata of those files, the 10.0.9 to 10.0.12 copies reference only CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo(string), and the 10.0.13, 10.0.14 and 10.0.15 copies reference only CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo(string, bool), the overload the fix calls, on both architectures. A byte search of every file in both 10.0.403-0 packages, including the files inside the nupkg archives they hold, finds the RequestLocalizationMiddleware name only in those two assemblies and the reference pack's XML documentation file. The range ends at 10.0.402-0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

Every dotnet-sdk-9 build carries one implementation copy of Microsoft.AspNetCore.Localization.dll, in the ASP.NET Core shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App/<version>, and one reference assembly with no implementation code under /usr/lib/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref/<version>; no other copy is present, including inside the nupkg archives. The shared framework version is 9.0.17 in 9.0.315-0, 9.0.18 in 9.0.316-0 and 9.0.316-1, 9.0.19 in 9.0.317-1, 9.0.20 in 9.0.318-0 and 9.0.318-1, 9.0.21 in 9.0.319-0, 9.0.22 in 9.0.320-0 and 9.0.23 in 9.0.321-0 and 9.0.321-1, the same on both architectures. Every copy records the dotnet/aspnetcore commit it was built from: the v9.0.17 to v9.0.20 tags in the builds up to 9.0.318-1, and the v9.0.21, v9.0.22 and v9.0.23 tags from 9.0.319-0 on, all three of which contain the fix commit. The range ends at 9.0.319-0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-96236 (GHSA-f4g7-52wc-p8x7) is an ASP.NET Core denial of service issue in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Localization: the request-localization fallback can add attacker-supplied synthetic culture names to the runtime's global cache, so unauthenticated requests can cause unbounded memory growth. Microsoft lists the ASP.NET Core 9.0 runtime packs, including linux-x64 and linux-arm64, as affected from 9.0.0 through 9.0.20 and fixed in 9.0.21: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f4g7-52wc-p8x7, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/484, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.21/9.0.21.md. The .NET 9 fix is dotnet/aspnetcore commit 271c3db316123fa62deb5fb21459b074983439c4 on release/9.0 ("Reject non-predefined cultures in request localization fallback"), which changes RequestLocalizationMiddleware.cs outside tests and test assets; it is in the v9.0.21 tag and not in v9.0.20: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/commit/271c3db316123fa62deb5fb21459b074983439c4. DHI dotnet-sdk-9 for Debian 13 packages Microsoft's .NET 9 SDK for Linux, which includes the .NET runtime and the ASP.NET Core shared framework. We scanned every package built from this source in the DHI Debian repository, 9.0.315-0, 9.0.316-0, 9.0.316-1, 9.0.317-1, 9.0.318-0, 9.0.318-1, 9.0.319-0, 9.0.320-0, 9.0.321-0 and 9.0.321-1, for amd64 and arm64 (the dotnet-sdk-9 and dotnet-sdk-9-oci-config packages; no debug-symbol packages are published), after verifying each against its index checksum and including the files inside the nupkg archives they hold. The dotnet-sdk-9-oci-config packages hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog.
